name: DsTau / NA65
full_name: DsTau / CERN NA65 tau-neutrino production experiment
summary: DsTau measures charm-meson production and decay chains that generate tau neutrinos, reducing a key source uncertainty for tau-neutrino interaction measurements. Data taking finished in 2023 and emulsion analysis continues. It measures the source process rather than detecting the neutrino itself.
physics_targets: Differential Ds production in proton-nucleus collisions
detection_principle: High-resolution emulsion layers record proton-nucleus interactions and the successive short flights in Ds-to-tau-to-daughter decays. Resolving the double-kink topology constrains the differential Ds production rate and hence the associated tau-neutrino flux.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The EPS-HEP 2025 collaboration presentation states that data taking was completed in 2023; emulsion scanning and physics analyses continue.

timeline.event: Experiment approved by CERN and feasibility study published

results.summary: Measured the proton interaction length in tungsten as 93.7 +/- 2.6 mm and compared charged-particle multiplicities with interaction models.

science_scope: A dedicated tau-neutrino source-calibration experiment. It is included because its central observable constrains the neutrino flux; it is not counted as a direct neutrino observation.
